To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ARFIMA processes are useful models for forecasting macroeconomic and financial series, and that they are especially useful when the forecast horizon is relatively long.
ARFIMA model forecasts are frequently better than AR, MA and ARMA forecasts, and that this is true for both recursive and rolling estimation procedures.
ARFIMA processes are useful for modeling and forecasting a variety of macroeconomic and financial series, and that ARFIMA modeling should be given serious consideration in future research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the ARFIMA model is a viable competitor to other time series models, in terms of out-of-sample predictive performance.
whether or not ARFIMA models should be considered for inclusion in the forecasting toolbox of applied economists and econometricians.
the question of whether the use of ARFIMA modeling can be justified in practice, given the potential computational and estimation problems associated with the use of such models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ARFIMA model are useful for forecasting, but that they are not the “best” models, as the best model depends on the data, the forecast horizon, and the estimation scheme used.
ARFIMA model are not always the best models for forecasting, but are sometimes significantly better than other models, especially when the data generating process (DGP) is fractional.
, in general, ARFIMA model outperform non-ARFIMAs, but the degree to which they do so varies from series to series, and from forecasting horizon to forecasting horizon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ARFIMA model is an excellent model for prediction of financial and macroeconomic series.
ARFIMA modeling is a potentially useful approach for modeling and forecasting macroeconomic and financial variables.
ARFIMA model provide a useful alternative to standard models in the context of out-of-sample prediction of financial and macroeconomic time series.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ARFIMA modeling should be seriously considered when forecasting macroeconomic and financial variables.
ARFIMA modeling should be considered in situations where standard models are unable to capture the long memory in a time series.
ARFIMA processes should be considered by practitioners and researchers alike, as they can often provide better out-of-sample forecasts than other commonly used models.
